title: Knock on the door frame yourself
step: Level 1, step 2 of 5 — the self-made sound
note: Written after the fact. This is one of the eight scenes drawn by hand through a chat window before the pipeline existed, so it had no spec; this one reconstructs it, because the picture is being redrawn for one reason only and everything else about it must survive unchanged. That reason is the door's window. The set was split 3–3 on it — four panes in the two exterior scenes and in door-greet-07-approach, two panes in this one, door-sound-01-setup, door-sound-03-name and door-sound-03-name-distant — and four is both what the live brief says in two places and what is physically true, since it is one door seen from either side. Four panes won, so the four two-pane pictures are being redrawn and this one goes first: it is the style:exemplar that nearly every other spec attaches, so until it is right every scene drawn against it inherits the wrong window. The exemplar here is door-stay-03-onestep rather than a file path — it is the same hall with the same closed door, already flat, already cool, and already four-pane, and naming the scene means this spec follows the approved master instead of a path that could go stale.
scene: Interior entry hall, close in beside the closed charcoal front door, which stands on the right of the frame. The handler is cropped by the TOP of the frame at the shoulders, so only her body from the shoulders down is in the picture — her head is not visible, and that crop is deliberate and must be kept. She stands square beside Lucy, close to the door, and her near arm is raised so her loosely closed fist is at the door frame beside the door, knocking on it. She is making the sound herself; nobody else is present and the door stays closed. Lucy sits square on the floor at the handler's side, close against her leg, facing the door with her ears up and attentive, calm and settled rather than excited. The black leash is clipped to the ring on Lucy's collar at the front of her neck, runs down and forward, and passes under the handler's near shoe, with a loose loop of slack lying on the oak floor. THE DOOR'S WINDOW: a four-pane grid in the upper half of the door — two panes across and two panes down, divided by one vertical bar and one horizontal bar, pale spruce foliage beyond. This is the same window seen in the exterior scenes and in door-stay-03-onestep, and it is four panes in every picture. Background: the closed charcoal door with its four-pane window, the woven doormat in front of it, one baseboard line, the lavender-grey wall, the oak floor. Nothing else in the room.
mustBeTrue: the door's window is a four-pane grid — two across and two down — the handler's raised fist is knocking on the door frame with her head cropped off by the top edge, Lucy sits square and close at her side facing the door, and the leash runs from Lucy's collar down under the handler's near shoe with a visible loop of slack on the floor.
